summary: The exact frozen T0 base exported all 8 declared FP32 LoRA gradients, reproduced the independent mean-loss adapter update exactly, left every base parameter unchanged, produced two byte-identical artifact directories, and passed every repository test.

guardrails.detail: Every frozen base parameter remained byte-equal after both update paths.
All 8 and only the 8 manifest-declared adapter tensors had finite FP32 gradients.
All 30 repository tests passed, including every pre-existing dense, browser-contract, coordinator, campaign, and release test.

findings.label: Adapter update parity established
findings.description: Worker-style summed gradients normalized and clipped once by the coordinator produced exactly the same adapter tensors as direct mean-loss backward.

findings.label: Portable deterministic artifact proof
findings.description: Two command-line exports were byte-identical and all six listed files passed sha256sum verification after enforcing LF checksum records.

findings.label: Numerical scope only
findings.description: This result validates Python semantics and artifact identity; it makes no claim about distributed throughput or model usefulness.

limitations: The proof uses deterministic synthetic T0 tokens and therefore does not establish useful adaptation quality.
No browser or native worker has yet computed the adapter gradients.
Adapter checkpoint restart, lease retry, multi-worker aggregation, evaluation, and release are not yet integrated.
RAM, quantized-base, and storage-offload behavior are outside this experiment.
